la:num:secundus.html:
sĕcundus, a, um, adj.
sequor
,
following.
(Acc. to sequor, I. B. 2.)
Prop., the following in time or order, the next to the first, the second (cf.: alter, proximus); absol.: si te secundo lumine hic offendero, the next morning, Enn. ap. : de tribus unum esset optandum...optimum est facere; secundum, nec facere nec pati; miserrimum digladiari semper, etc.,the next best,; cf.: id secundum erat de tribus,: aliquem obligare secundo sacramento, priore amisso, etc.,; cf.: prioribus equitum partibus secundis additis,: Roma condita est secundo anno Olympiadis septimae,: Olympias secunda et sexagesima,: oriens incendium belli Punici secundi,: aliquem secundum heredem instituere, the second or substituted heir, if the first-named die or refuse the inheritance, ; so, heres,; : mensa,the second course, dessert,; ; ; ; ; ; : Germania,Lower Germany,.—Subst.: sĕcundae, ārum, f. (sc. membranae), the after-birth, secundines: partus,: non magis pertinere quam secundas ad editum infantem,; ; ; : secundae partūs,; ; .—
Trop.
Following, next, second in rank, value, etc.; with ad: quorum ordo proxime accedit, ut secundus sit ad regium principatum,.—With ab: potentiā secundus a rege,; with which cf.: secundus a Romulo conditor urbis Romanae,; and: Ajax, heros ab Achille secundus,: qui honos secundus a rege erat,.—Absol.: nil majus generatur ipso (Jove), Nec viget quicquam simile aut secundum, : tu (Juppiter) secundo Caesare regnes,; corresp. to maxime: maxime vellem...secundo autem loco, etc.,; cf.: me maxime consolatur spes, etc....facile secundo loco me consolatur recordatio, etc.,: cotes Creticae diu maximam laudem habuere, secundam Laconicae,.—With dat.: nulli Campanorum secundus vinctus ad mortem rapior, Weissenb. ad loc.: regio spatio locorum nulli earum gentium secunda,; : secundus sibi, non par,: secunda nobilitas Falerno agro,: bonitas amomo pallido,.—With abl., ; cf. supra.—
With the prevailing idea of subjection or inferiority, secondary, subordinate, inferior; absol.: secundae sortis ingenium,only of the second grade,: moneri velle ac posse secunda virtus est,; cf.: (servi) quasi secundum hominum genus sunt,: vivit siliquis et pane secundo (i. e. secundario), (cf.: secundarius panis,; ): tenue argentum venaeque secundae,: haec fuit altera persona Thebis, sed tamen secunda ita, ut proxima esset Epaminondae,. —With abl.: haud ulli veterum virtute secundus,inferior,.—With inf.: nec vertere cuiquam Frena secundus Halys,.—Esp., in phrase partes secundae, second parts, inferior parts: in actoribus Graecis, ille qui est secundarum aut tertiarum partium,: ut credas partis mimum tractare secundas,.—With ab: hic erit a mensis fine secunda dies,the last day but one of the month,. —As subst.: sĕcundae, ārum, f. (sc. partes), the second or inferior parts: Spinther secundarum tertiarum Pamphilus,; : Q. Arrius, qui fuit M. Crassi quasi secundarum,; so, secundas sortiri,: ferre,: deferre alicui,: agere,.—
(Acc. to sequor, II.)
Prop., naut. t. t., of currents of water, etc., favorable, fair (as following the course of the vessel): secundo flumine ad Lutetiam iter facere coepit,i. e. down the stream,; so, Tiberi,: amni,: fluvio,: aqua,; cf.: totā rate in secundam aquam labente,with the current,: et ventum et aestum uno tempore nactus secundum,; so, aestu,: mari,; and, poet.: (Neptunus) curru secundo,speeding along,: secundo amne,: navigatio,.—Esp., of winds: in portum vento secundo, velo passo pervenit,; cf.: cum videam navem secundis ventis cursum tenentem suum,; so, ventus,; ; ; cf. aquilo,.—Sup.: cum secundissimo vento cursum teneret,.—Of sails (trop.): des ingenio vela secunda meo,.—
Transf., with, according to any thing: austri anniversarii secundo sole flant, i. e. according to the course of the sun, Nigid. ap. : squama secunda (opp. adversa), as we say, with the grain, i. e. so as to offer no resistance to the hand when it is passed from the head to the tail, id. ap. .—
Trop., favorable, propitious, fortunate (opp. adversus); absol.: secundo populo aliquid facere,with the consent of the people,; so, concio,; cf.: voluntas concionis,: admurmurationes cuncti senatūs,: rumor, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 260 Vahl.); : clamor,: aures,; ; : praesentibus ac secundis diis,; so, dis auspicibus et Junone secundā,; and: secundo Marte ruat,: adi pede sacra secundo,; 10, 255: auspicia,; cf. avis, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 82 Vahl.); and in poet. hypallage: haruspex,: scitus, secunda loquens in tempore, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 251 Vahl.): res (opp. adversae), ; so,; ; ; ; cf. fortunae (opp. adversae),; and tempora (opp. adversi casus),; so, res, Enn. ap. Müll. (Ann. v. 357 Vahl.); ; (with prosperitates); ; : fortunae, Cato ap. Fest. s. v. parsi, p. 242 Müll.; : proelia,: motus Galliae,successful,; and: belli exitus,: consilium,: labores,.—Comp.: reliqua militia secundiore famā fuit,.—Sup.: secundissima proelia,.— With dat.: secunda (sc. verba) irae,i. e. increasing, promoting it,.—Comp.: secundiore equitum proelio nostris,.—Sup.: tres leges secundissimas plebei, adversas nobilitati tulit,: omnia secundissima nobis, adversissima illis accidisse videntur, Caes. ap. , B.—As subst.: sĕcunda, ōrum, n., favorable circumstances, good fortune: sperat infestis, metuit secundis Alteram sortem,: age, me in tuis secundis respice,: omnium secundorum adversorumque causes in deos vertere,: in secundis sapere et consulere,: nimius homo inter secunda,; ; : nemo confidat nimium secundis,: poscunt fidem secunda,: secunda non habent unquam modum,.

senses: according to (with object in accusative case)
fortunate, lucky, victorious, successful (of battle--secundum proelium)

senses: just after, following, next to, subsequently to

la:prep:secundum.html:
sĕcundum, adv. and prep.
sequor
.
Adv.
After, behind: Am. Age, i ut secundum. So. Sequor, subsequor te, .—
Afterwards, in the next place, secondly (so very rare): animadvertendum primum, quibus de causis constituerint paces; secundum, quā fide eas coluerint, Varr. ap. (but secundum is a false reading for iterum in ; ).—
Prep. with acc.
Prop.
In space.
Following after, i.e. after, behind (ante-class.): ite hac secundum vos me,: nos secundum ferre haec,after us, behind us,: secundum ipsam aram aurum abscondidi, id. Fragm. ap. P.—
Following an extension in space, i. e. by, along (class.): cum leno secundum parietem transversus iret, Müll.: quae (legiones) iter secundum mare superum faciunt,: sex legiones ad oppidum Gergoviam secundum flumen Elaver duxit,: quid illuc est hominum secundum litus?: hoc genus saepes fieri secundum vias publicas solent et secundum amnes,: secundum flumen,

; cf.: castra secundum mare haberet,: vulnus accepit in capite secundum aurem, Sulp. ap. : centaurium secundum fontes nascitur,.—

In time, succession, rank, value, etc., immediately after, after, next to (class.): secundum vindemiam, ubi vites ablaqueantur,: secundum ludos,; cf.: tua ratio est, ut secundum binos ludos mihi respondere incipias: mea, ut ante primos ludos comperendinem,; so, comitia,: hunc diem,: aequinoctium vernum,: proelium,: quietem,after going to sleep, while asleep, in a dream,; so ; ; : secundum patrem tu es pater proximus,; cf.: proxime et secundum deos homines hominibus maxime utiles esse possunt,: ille mihi secundum te et liberos nostros ita est, ut sit paene par,: secundum te nihil est mihi amicius solitudine,: qui secundum deos nomen Romanum veneretur,: in actione secundum vocem vultus valet,; : secundum ea quaero, servarisne, etc.,; so, secundum ea,; cf. (with preceding maxime) Fabri ad loc.—
Fig.
Agreeably to, in accordance with, according to (class.): tigna prona et fastigata, ut secundum naturam fluminis procumberent,; cf.: secundum naturam vivere,; and: facilius esse secundum naturam, quam contra eam, vivere,: collaudavi secundum facta et virtutes tuas,: duumviros secundum legem facio,; so, legem,; : rationem,: secundum consuetudinem praedatum ire,.—
Pregn., according to the will of, in favor of, to the advantage of: nuntiat populo, pontifices secundum se decrevisse...multa secundum causam nostram disputavit,: de absente secundum praesentem judicare,: secundum eam (partem) litem judices dare,: rei, quae undique secundum nos sit,: post principia belli secundum Flavianos,.

sēcum = cum se; v. cum, II.

la:adj:securus.html:
sē-cūrus, a, um, adj.
se = sine and cura
, i. q. non or nibil curans,
free from care, careless, unconcerned, untroubled, fearless, quiet, easy, composed.
Lit.
In a good sense (class.; cf. tutus); constr. absol., with de, ab, gen., or a rel.-clause: ut, meis ab tergo tutis, securus bellum Nabidi inferam,: securus solutusque,; (with otiosus),: securus Hermippus Temnum proficiscitur,: sine militis usu Mollia securae peragebant otia gentes,; ; : non secura quidem, fausto tamen omine laeta Mater abit templo,; cf.: a non securo Eumene,: Ceres natā secura receptā,easy now that she had found,; cf. (v. infra, b.): de linguā Latinā securi es animi,: de bello Romano,: de facilitate credentis,: securos vos ab hac parte reddemus, Planc. ap. ; ; so, ab hac parte,.—Comp.: securior ab Samnitibus,: Romani securi pro salute de gloriā certabant,: aut pro vobis sollicitior, aut pro me securior,.— With gen. (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): ne sis secura futuri,; so, suis (gen. of sus), : extremi sepulcri,: pelagi atque mei,unconcerned about,: amorum germanae,; 10, 326: poenae,: tam parvae observationis (Cicero),: odii,: potentiae,: nec securam incrementi sui patiebatur esse Italiam,: qui (motus) Campaniam numquam securam hujus mali...vastavit,: quem (rogum) uxoria pietas mortis secura conscendit,, ext. 14: his persuadet, ut securo fugae suae Eumeni superveniant,: periculi,: discurrunt securi casus ejus, qui supervenit ignaris, (v. infra, b.). —With rel.-clause: gestit nummum in loculos demittere, post hoc Securus, cadat an recto stet fabula talo,; (opp. laboret); .— With ne and subj.: ne quis etiam errore labatur vestrum quoque, non sum securus,.—
Of inanim. things.
Free from care, untroubled, tranquil, serene, cheerful, bright (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): deos securum agere aevum,; ; : quies (leti),; : otia,: dies,: merum,: mensa,: convivia,: artus (Herculis),: gaudia nato recepto,: summa malorum,careless,: olus,i.e. of the careless idler, et saep.; : causae,: vox securae claritatis,: tempus securius,more free from care,; cf.: securior materia, et saep.: securos ab eo metu somnos,. —With gen.: vota secura repulsae,safe against,.—
Poet., that frees from care or anxiety: latices, (securos ab effectu, Serv. ad l. l.).—
In a bad sense, careless, reckless, heedless, negligent (post-Aug. and very rare): reus,; cf. ; .—Of abstract things: castrensis jurisdictio, easy, off-hand (shortly after, opp. gravis, intentus), : luxus,.—
Transf., object., of a thing or place, free from danger, safe, secure (not till after the Aug. period, and rare for the class. tutus): hostis levis et velox et repentinus, qui nullum usquam tempus, nullum locum quietum aut securum esse sineret,: domus,: Tripolim securissimam reddidit,: securiorem,: quorum (hominum) ea natura est, ut secura velint,safety, security,fin.—With gen.: subitā inundatione Tiberis non modo jacentia et plana urbis loca sed secura ejusmodi casuum implevit,secure from such accidents,.—Adv., in two forms,
sē-cūrē.
(Acc. to I.) Carelessly, heedlessly, fearlessly, unconcernedly, quietly (not ante-Aug.): lente ac secure aliquid ferre,; (with neglegenter); ; ext. al.—Comp., .—
(Acc. to II.) Safely, securely, .—
sēcūrĭter (late Lat.), .

la:noun:securis.gloss: an axe, hatchet with a broad edge
senses: an axe, hatchet with a broad edge
la:noun:securis.html:
sĕcūris, is (acc. securim, ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; cf. :
securem,; ; ; ; Varr. ap. ; , ext. 3; 3, 2, ext. 1; ; ; ; cf. ; abl. securi, ; ; ; ; 2, 5, 50, § 133; ; ; ; ; et saep.: secure,; ), f.
seco
, an axe or hatchet with a broad edge (cf. bipennis).
In gen., as a domestic utensil, ; ; : rustica,—For felling trees, ; ; ; ; ; .—For hewing stones in the quarries, . —For fighting, a battle-axe, ; ; ; 7, 184; 7, 627; : anceps,a two-edged axe, (just before, bipennifer).—For slaying animals for sacrifice, ; ; ; .—As the cutting edge of a vine-dresser's bill, et saep.—
In partic.
Lit., an executioner's axe, for beheading criminals

(borne by the lictors in the fasces; v. fascis): missi lictores ad sumendum supplicium nudatos virgis caedunt securique feriunt,i. e. behead them,. 5; so, securi ferire,; : percutere,; ; : strictae in principum colla secures,: necare,: securibus cervices subicere, (cf. infra, B.); : Publicola statim secures de fascibus demi jussit,; cf. ; : nec sumit aut ponit secures Arbitrio popularis aurae,: saevumque securi Aspice Torquatum (as having caused his own son to be executed),.—Comically, in a double sense, acc. to I.: te, cum securi, caudicali praeficio provinciae,: securis Tenedia,; ; v. Tenedos.—

Trop.
A blow, death-blow, etc.: graviorem rei publicae infligere securim,to give a death-blow,; cf.: quam te securim putas injecisse petitioni tuae, cum? etc. (just before: plaga est injecta petitioni tuae),.—
With reference to the axe in the fasces, authority, dominion, sovereignty.
Usu. in plur.: Gallia securibus subjecta, perpetuā premitur servitute, i. e. to Roman supremacy, * ; cf.: vacui a securibus et tributis,: consulis inperium hic primus saevasque secures Accipiet,: Medus Albanas timet secures, i. e. the Roman authority or dominion, : ostendam multa securibus recidenda,.—
In sing. (poet.): Germania colla Romanae praebens animosa securi,.

la:verb:secundo.html:
sĕcundo, āre, v. a.
id.
. *
To direct favorably, to adjust, adapt, accommodate: tempus ei rei secundas, dub.—
To favor, further, second (poet. and in post-Aug. prose; syn.: faveo, adjuvo): jam liquidum nautis aura secundat iter,aura aquas,.—Absol.: secundante vento,the wind being favorable,: cum secundante vento celeriter advolare,: di nostra incepta secundent,: votum (deus),: cursum (Fortuna),: eventus,: rite secundarent visus, that they would prosper well the tokens, i. e. secure them a favorable issue, ; so, visa,; .

la:verb:secerno.gloss: to put apart, sunder, sever, separate, divide
senses: to put apart, sunder, sever, separate, divide
to set aside, reject, exclude, pull aside
la:verb:secerno.html:
sē-cerno, crēvi, crētum, 3 (old
inf. secernier, ), v. a.
Lit., to put apart, to sunder, sever, separate (freq. and class.; not in Cæs.; cf.: sepono, sejungo, secludo); constr. with simple acc., or with ab aliquā re; less freq. ex aliquā re;poet. with abl.
With simple acc.: quae non animalia solum Corpora sejungunt, sed terras ac mare totum Secernunt,: seorsum partem utramque,: arietes, quibus sis usurus ad feturam, bimestri tempore ante secernendum, (cf. infra, β): stamen secernit harundo,: sparsos sine ordine flores Secernunt calathis,separate in baskets,: nihil (praedae) in publicum secernendo augenti rem privatam militi favit,setting apart for the public treasury,; cf.: Juppiter illa piae secrevit litora genti,hath set apart for the pious race,: inde pares centum denos secrevit in orbes Romulus,separated, divided,.—
With ab or (less freq.) with ex, and poet. with abl.: a terris altum secernere caelum,: ab aëre caelum,: Europen ab Afro (medius liquor),: muro denique secernantur a nobis,: inermes ab armatis,: militem a populo (in spectaculis),: se a bonis,; cf.: se ab Etruscis,.—In the part. perf.: antequam incipiat admissura fieri, mares a feminis secretos habeant, (cf. supra, α); so, saepta ab aliis,: manus a nobis,; : sphaera ab aethereā conjunctione,: sucus a reliquo cibo,: bilis ab eo cibo, al.: secreti ab aliis ad tribunos adducuntur,; : secretis alterius ab altero criminibus,; : se e grege imperatorum,: unum e praetextatis compluribus,: monile ex omni gazā,: me gelidum nemus Nympharumque leves chori Secernunt populo,separate, distinguish,.—
Trop., to separate, disjoin, part, dissociate (syn.: internosco, distinguo).
With simple acc.: hosce ego homines excipio et secerno libenter,set apart,.—
With ab, or poet. with abl.: ut venustas et pulchritudo corporis secerni non potest a valetudine; sic, etc.,: animum a corpore,: tertium genus (laudationum) a praeceptis nostris,; cf.: ipsam pronuntiationem ab oratore,: dicendi facultatem a majore vitae laude, : sua a publicis consiliis,: haec a probris ac sceleribus ejus, et saep.: cur me a ceteris clarissimis viris in hoc officio secernas,: publica privatis, sacra profanis,.—
To distinguish, discern: blandum amicum a vero,: non satis acute, quae sunt secernenda, distinguit,: nec natura potest justo secernere iniquum, Dividit ut bona diversis, fugienda petendis,: turpi honestum,.—
To set aside, reject: cum reus frugalissimum quemque secerneret,: minus idoneos senatores,.—Hence, sēcrē-tus, a, um, P. a., severed, separated; hence, separate, apart (as an adj. not freq. till after the Aug. period; not in Cic.; syn.: sejunctus, seclusus).
In gen.: ne ducem suum, neve secretum imperium propriave signa haberent, miscuit manipulos, etc.,: electa (uva defertur) in secretam corbulam,: arva,; Müll.—
In partic.
Of places or things pertaining to them, out of the way, retired, remote, lonely, solitary, secret (syn.: solus, remotus, arcanus): secreta petit loca, balnea vitat,: locus (opp. celeber),: montes,: silva,: litora,: pars domus (the gynaeceum),; cf. in sup.: secretissimus locus (navis),: vastum ubique silentium, secreti colles, solitary, i. e. abandoned, deserted by the enemy, = deserti, : iter (with semita),solitary,; cf. quies,.—Of persons and transactions, private, secret: invadit secretissimos tumultus,: vacuis porticibus secretus agitat,: est aliquis ex secretis studiis fructus,private studies,; so, studia (opp. forum),: disputationes,: contentio, et saep. —Hence,
Subst.: sēcrētum, i, n., retirement, solitude, secrecy; a solitude, solitary place, retreat (syn.: solitudo, secessus); sing.: cum stilus secreto gaudeat atque omnes arbitros reformidet,: secreti longi causā,: altum abditumque secretum, Phn. Ep. 2, 17, 22: dulce,; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; .— Plur.: se a vulgo et scaenā in secreta removere,: horrendaeque procul secreta Sibyllae,; ; ; : dulcis secretorum comes (eloquentia),: cameli solitudines aut secreta certe petunt,.—Comp.: haec pars Suevorum in secretiora Germaniae porrigitur,into the more remote parts,. —
Absol.: in secreto, in a secret place, secretly: tempus in secreto lbi tereret,: reus in secreto agebatur,.—
That is removed from acquaintance (cf. abditus), hidden, concealed, secret: secreta ducis pectora,: secretas advocat artes,: ars,: litterae (with familiares),: carmina (the Sibylline odes),: libidines,: quaedam imperii pignora,.—With ab: nec quicquam secretum alter ab altero haberent,.—Comp.: libertus ex secretioribus ministeriis,: praemia (opp. publica largitio),: aliud (nomen),: vitium stomachi,.—Poet. for the adv. secreto: tu (Anna) secreta pyram tecto interiore Erige,in secret, secretly,; cf.: stridere secreta divisos aure susurros,secretly in each one's ear,.—Hence,
Subst.: sēcrētum, i, n., something secret, secret conversation; a mystery, secret: secretum petenti non nisi adhibito filio dedit,; : illuc me persecutus secretum petit,a secret interview,: petito secreto futura aperit,.— Piur.: crebra cum amicis secreta habere,: animi secreta proferuntur,: nulla lex jubet amicorum secreta non eloqui,: omnium secreta rimari,: horribile secretum,; fin.; ; : uxor omnis secreti capacissima,; —Concr.: lucos ac nemora consecrant deorumque nominibus appellant secretum illud, quod solā reverentiā vident,that mysterious being,fin.—Plur.: introitus, aperta, secreta velut in annales referebat,; cf.: gens non astuta aperit adhuc secreta pectoris licentia joci,: oratio animi secreta detegit,; ; fin.; 6, 3; ; ; ; et saep.—Concr.: (Minerva) hanc legem dederat, sua ne secreta viderent,i. e. the mysteries,; ; cf.: secretiora quaedam,magic arts,: in secretis ejus reperti sunt duo libelli,among his private papers,.—
Pregn., separate from what is common, i. e. uncommon, rare, recondite (perh. only in the two foll. passages of Quint.): (figurae) secretae et extra vulgarem usum positae, etc.,: interpretatio linguae secretioris, quas Graeci γλώσσας vocant, i. e. of the more uncommon words, (for which: glossemata id est voces minus usitatas,).—
In Lucr., of any thing separated from what belongs to it, i. e. wanting, deprived of, without something; with abl. or gen.: nec porro secreta cibo natura animantum Propagare genus possit (corresp. to sine imbribus),: (corpora) secreta teporis Sunt ac frigoris omnino calidique vaporis (corresp. to spoliata colore),. —Hence, adv., in three forms: secreto (class.), secrete (post-class.), and secretim (late Lat. and very rare). *
(Acc. to A.) Apart, by itself, separately: de quibus (hortis) suo loco dicam secretius,. —
(Acc. to B. 2.) In secret, secretly; without witnesses; in private.
sēcrē-tō: mirum, quid solus secum secreto ille agat,: secreto illum adjutabo,: secreto hoc audi,: nescio quid secreto velle loqui te Aiebas mecum,: secreto te huc seduxi,: facere,; ; ; ; Cael. ap. : secreto ab aliis,: secreto agere cum aliquo,; ; ; ; .—
sēcrētē, ; —
Comp.: secretius emittitur inflatio,. —
sēcrētim, .

la:other:Secundus.html:
sĕcundus, a, um, adj.
sequor
,
following.
(Acc. to sequor, I. B. 2.)
Prop., the following in time or order, the next to the first, the second (cf.: alter, proximus); absol.: si te secundo lumine hic offendero, the next morning, Enn. ap. : de tribus unum esset optandum...optimum est facere; secundum, nec facere nec pati; miserrimum digladiari semper, etc.,the next best,; cf.: id secundum erat de tribus,: aliquem obligare secundo sacramento, priore amisso, etc.,; cf.: prioribus equitum partibus secundis additis,: Roma condita est secundo anno Olympiadis septimae,: Olympias secunda et sexagesima,: oriens incendium belli Punici secundi,: aliquem secundum heredem instituere, the second or substituted heir, if the first-named die or refuse the inheritance, ; so, heres,; : mensa,the second course, dessert,; ; ; ; ; ; : Germania,Lower Germany,.—Subst.: sĕcundae, ārum, f. (sc. membranae), the after-birth, secundines: partus,: non magis pertinere quam secundas ad editum infantem,; ; ; : secundae partūs,; ; .—
Trop.
Following, next, second in rank, value, etc.; with ad: quorum ordo proxime accedit, ut secundus sit ad regium principatum,.—With ab: potentiā secundus a rege,; with which cf.: secundus a Romulo conditor urbis Romanae,; and: Ajax, heros ab Achille secundus,: qui honos secundus a rege erat,.—Absol.: nil majus generatur ipso (Jove), Nec viget quicquam simile aut secundum, : tu (Juppiter) secundo Caesare regnes,; corresp. to maxime: maxime vellem...secundo autem loco, etc.,; cf.: me maxime consolatur spes, etc....facile secundo loco me consolatur recordatio, etc.,: cotes Creticae diu maximam laudem habuere, secundam Laconicae,.—With dat.: nulli Campanorum secundus vinctus ad mortem rapior, Weissenb. ad loc.: regio spatio locorum nulli earum gentium secunda,; : secundus sibi, non par,: secunda nobilitas Falerno agro,: bonitas amomo pallido,.—With abl., ; cf. supra.—
With the prevailing idea of subjection or inferiority, secondary, subordinate, inferior; absol.: secundae sortis ingenium,only of the second grade,: moneri velle ac posse secunda virtus est,; cf.: (servi) quasi secundum hominum genus sunt,: vivit siliquis et pane secundo (i. e. secundario), (cf.: secundarius panis,; ): tenue argentum venaeque secundae,: haec fuit altera persona Thebis, sed tamen secunda ita, ut proxima esset Epaminondae,. —With abl.: haud ulli veterum virtute secundus,inferior,.—With inf.: nec vertere cuiquam Frena secundus Halys,.—Esp., in phrase partes secundae, second parts, inferior parts: in actoribus Graecis, ille qui est secundarum aut tertiarum partium,: ut credas partis mimum tractare secundas,.—With ab: hic erit a mensis fine secunda dies,the last day but one of the month,. —As subst.: sĕcundae, ārum, f. (sc. partes), the second or inferior parts: Spinther secundarum tertiarum Pamphilus,; : Q. Arrius, qui fuit M. Crassi quasi secundarum,; so, secundas sortiri,: ferre,: deferre alicui,: agere,.—
(Acc. to sequor, II.)
Prop., naut. t. t., of currents of water, etc., favorable, fair (as following the course of the vessel): secundo flumine ad Lutetiam iter facere coepit,i. e. down the stream,; so, Tiberi,: amni,: fluvio,: aqua,; cf.: totā rate in secundam aquam labente,with the current,: et ventum et aestum uno tempore nactus secundum,; so, aestu,: mari,; and, poet.: (Neptunus) curru secundo,speeding along,: secundo amne,: navigatio,.—Esp., of winds: in portum vento secundo, velo passo pervenit,; cf.: cum videam navem secundis ventis cursum tenentem suum,; so, ventus,; ; ; cf. aquilo,.—Sup.: cum secundissimo vento cursum teneret,.—Of sails (trop.): des ingenio vela secunda meo,.—
Transf., with, according to any thing: austri anniversarii secundo sole flant, i. e. according to the course of the sun, Nigid. ap. : squama secunda (opp. adversa), as we say, with the grain, i. e. so as to offer no resistance to the hand when it is passed from the head to the tail, id. ap. .—
Trop., favorable, propitious, fortunate (opp. adversus); absol.: secundo populo aliquid facere,with the consent of the people,; so, concio,; cf.: voluntas concionis,: admurmurationes cuncti senatūs,: rumor, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 260 Vahl.); : clamor,: aures,; ; : praesentibus ac secundis diis,; so, dis auspicibus et Junone secundā,; and: secundo Marte ruat,: adi pede sacra secundo,; 10, 255: auspicia,; cf. avis, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 82 Vahl.); and in poet. hypallage: haruspex,: scitus, secunda loquens in tempore, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 251 Vahl.): res (opp. adversae), ; so,; ; ; ; cf. fortunae (opp. adversae),; and tempora (opp. adversi casus),; so, res, Enn. ap. Müll. (Ann. v. 357 Vahl.); ; (with prosperitates); ; : fortunae, Cato ap. Fest. s. v. parsi, p. 242 Müll.; : proelia,: motus Galliae,successful,; and: belli exitus,: consilium,: labores,.—Comp.: reliqua militia secundiore famā fuit,.—Sup.: secundissima proelia,.— With dat.: secunda (sc. verba) irae,i. e. increasing, promoting it,.—Comp.: secundiore equitum proelio nostris,.—Sup.: tres leges secundissimas plebei, adversas nobilitati tulit,: omnia secundissima nobis, adversissima illis accidisse videntur, Caes. ap. , B.—As subst.: sĕcunda, ōrum, n., favorable circumstances, good fortune: sperat infestis, metuit secundis Alteram sortem,: age, me in tuis secundis respice,: omnium secundorum adversorumque causes in deos vertere,: in secundis sapere et consulere,: nimius homo inter secunda,; ; : nemo confidat nimium secundis,: poscunt fidem secunda,: secunda non habent unquam modum,.

la:adv:secundo.html:
sĕcundō, adv.
secundus
.
Secondly, in the second place (rare): equidem primum, ut honore dignus essem, maxime semper laboravi; secundo, ut existimarer; tertium mihi fuit illud quod, etc.,; so, primo ... secundo, (acc. to P., also used by Cato).—
For the second time: Pontica legio cum fossam circumire secundo conata esset, Auct. B. Alex. 40; ; ; .—
Twice: lavit ad diem septimo aestate vel sexto, hieme secundo vel tertio, Treb. Gall. 17.

la:verb:secedo.gloss: to withdraw, to secede, to separate oneself, to shut oneself off, to seek distance
senses: to withdraw, to secede, to separate oneself, to shut oneself off, to seek distance
la:verb:secedo.html:
sē-cēdo, cessi, cessum, 3, v. n.,
to go apart, go away, separate, withdraw (class.; not in Cæs.; but cf. secessio).
Lit.
In gen., absol.: secedant improbi, secernant se a bonis,; : prosecutus eram viatico secedentem,: abite et de viā secedite,: de coetu,: a vestro potui secedere lusu,: utinam nostro secedere corpore possem!.—
Poet., of inanim. subjects, to remove, withdraw; and in the perf., to be distant: (luna) quantum solis secedit ab orbe,: ab imis terra,: (villa) decem et septem milibus passuum ab urbe secessit,; Pall. et Cell. 63.—
In partic.
To go aside, withdraw,

retire: secede huc nunc jam procul,; so, huc,; ; : in abditam partem aedium,: in utraque latera (cohortes),: ad deliberandum,: ad consultandum,: lex Spartana vetat secedere amantes, (4, 13), 21: secedit humumque Effodit,. —

In post-Aug. authors (esp. in Suet.), to retire from public into private life; absol.: integrā aetate ac valetudine statuit repente secedere seque e medio quam longissime amovere,: illuc e comitatu suo,; so : ab Urbe,: in insulam, etc.,; ; ; cf. Rhodum,.—
To seek the exclusive society of any one, to retire from the world: ad optimos viros,. —
Polit., to separate one's self by rebellion, to revolt, secede (syn.: deficio, descisco): ut anno XVI. post reges exactos propter nimiam dominationem potentium secederent, Orell.: saepe ipsa plebes armata a patribus secessit,; : injussu consulum in Sacrum Montem secessisse,to have marched out in rebellion,; so, in Sacrum Montem,; : in Janiculum (plebs),.—
Trop. (very rare; perh. only poet. and in post-Aug. prose): antequam ego incipio secedere et aliā parte considere,to dissent from the opinion,: a fesso corpore sensus,: qui solitarius separatusque a communi malo civitatis secesserit,has withdrawn himself,: cum ad stilum secedet,shall give himself up to writing,: in te ipse secede,retire within yourself,.

la:noun:secessus.html:
sēcessus, ūs, m.
secedo
,
a going away, departure, separation (not ante-Aug.).
In gen. (very rare): avium,: quasi quodam secessu mentis atque animi facto a corpore,.—
In partic.
(Acc. to secedo, I. B. 1.) Retirement, solitude (the prevailing signif. of the word; syn. solitudo).
Lit.: carmina secessum scribentis et otia quaerunt,; cf.: medium tempus

in otio secessuque egit, : in secessu ruris sui Sabini, id. Fragm. Vit. Hor. fin.: silentium et secessus non semper possunt contingere,; ; ; ; ; ; ; : specie secessus exul,: unus e senatoribus Rhodii secessus comes,: gratum litus amoeni secessus, et saep.—

Transf., a retreat, recess: est in secessu longo locus, etc.,; ; ; cf. ; ; ; ; ; in plur., ; ; ; ; ; al.—Of a privy, .—
Trop. (very rare): ideoque mihi videtur M. Tullius tantum intulisse eloquentiae lumen, quod in hos quoque studiorum secessus excurrit, into these remote departments of study (i. e. remote from forensic debates), : in secessu quam in fronte beatior,in his own mind, inwardly,ext.—
(Acc. to secedo, I. B. 2.) For the usual secessio (II.), a political secession: iratae plebis secessus,.—
A place of retirement, privy, drain (late Lat.), ; .

la:verb:seco.html:
sĕco, cŭi, ctum (
part. fut. secaturus, ), 1, v. a.
root sak-, to cut; whence securis, sĕcula, serra (secra), segmen, sexus, saxum, etc.; cf. sīca, and Gr. κείω, κεάζω, σχίζω
, to cut, cut off, cut up (class.; syn.: caedo, scindo).
Lit.
In gen.: leges duodecim tabularum, si plures forent, quibus rens esset judicatus, secare, si vellent, atque partiri corpus addicti sibi hominis permiserunt,; cf.: et judicatos in partes secari a creditoribus leges erant,: cape cultrum, seca Digitum vel aurem,: omne animal secari ac dividi potest, nullum est eorum individuum,: pabulum secari non posse, be cut, mown, * ; so, sectae herbae,: gallinam,to cut to pieces,: placenta,: alicui collum gladio suā dexterā,: palatum,to divide,: tergora in frusta,: dona auro gravia sectoque elephanto, i. e. of carved, wrought ivory (an imitation of the Homeric πριστὸς ἐλέφας, Od. 18, 196), : marmora,: sectis nitebat marmoribus, ; so absol.: nec ideo ferrum secandi vim non perdidit,: prave sectus unguis,: secti lapides,. —
In partic.
Med. t. t., to cut surgically; to operate on; to cut off or out, amputate, excise, etc.: in corpore si quid ejusmodi est, quod reliquo corpori noceat, id uri secarique patimur,; cf.: saevitia secandi,; so, membra,: vomicam,: varices Mario, (for which, exciditur, ); cf. of the same: C. Marius cum secaretur, ut supra dixi, principio vetuit se alligari; nec quisquam ante Marium solutus dicitur esse sectus,was cut, operated upon,: servum,.—
To cut, castrate (very rare): puer avari sectus arte mangonis,; so, sectus Gallus (corresp. to eviratus),.—
Transf. (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
To scratch, tear, wound, hurt, injure (cf. caedo, II.): ambo (postes) ab infimo tarmes secat,the worms are gnawing them, they are wormeaten,: luctantis acuto ne secer ungui,lest I should be torn,; cf.: rigido sectas invenit ungue genas,: teneras plantas tibi (glacies),: corpora vepres,: crura (sentes),: pete ferro Corpus et intorto verbere terga seca,cut, lacerate,; so, sectus flagellis,: loris,: si quem podagra secat,gnaws, torments,; imitated by Martial: podagra cheragraque secatur Gaius,.—
Like the Gr. τέμνειν, and our to cut, i. e.,
To divide, cleave, separate (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): quos (populos) secans interluit Allia,: medios Aethiopas (Nilus),: medios agros (Tiberis),: medium agmen (Turnus),: agrum (limes),: caelum (zonae),: sectus orbis,; cf.: in longas orbem qui secuere vias,.—
With the idea of motion, to cut through, i. e. to run, sail, fly, swim, go, etc., through: delphinum similes, qui per maria umida nando Carpathium Libycumque secant,cut through, cleave,: aequor,: pontum,: aequor Puppe,: fretum puppe,; cf.: vada nota (amnis),: ales avis ... geminis secat aëra pennis,: aethera pennis (avis),; : auras (cornus),: ventos (Cyllenia proles),: sub nubibus arcum (Iris), et saep.— Secare viam (vias), the Gr. τέμνειν ὁδόν,to take one's way, to travel a road: ille viam secat ad naves,: hinc velut diversae secari coeperunt viae,.—
Trop. (acc. to I. C. 1. and 2.). *
To cut up, lash in speaking, i.e. to censure, satirize: secuit Lucilius Urbem,.—
To divide (not freq. till after the Aug. per.): cum causas in plura genera secuerunt,: haec in plures partes,; cf.: scrupulose in partes sectā divisionis diligentiā,: quae natura singularia sunt secant (corresp. to divido),: sectae ad tenuitatem suam vires (just before: distinguendo. dividendo),.—Hence, in Hor., like dirimo (II.), of disputes, to cut off, i.e. to decide them: quo multae magnaeque secantur judice lites,: magnas res, to cure (as it were, by a light operation), .—And once in Verg.: secare spem (the figure borrowed from the phrases secare mare, auras, viam): quae cuique est fortuna hodie, quam quisque secat spem, whatever hope each follows, i. e. indulges in, entertains, (secat, sequitur, tenet, habet; ut: Ille viam secat ad naves,: unde et sectas dicimus, habitus animorum et instituta philosophiae circa disciplinam, Serv.).

la:verb:secludo.html:
sē-clūdo, si, sum, 3,
v. a. [claudo], to shut off, shut in a separate place, to shut up, seclude (rare but class.; syn.: secerno, sejungo).
Lit.: incientes (oves) secludere, to shut up, confine, Varr, R. R. 2, 2, 8; : illuc eum rapiam, ubi non seclusa aliqua aquula teneatur, sed unde universum flumen erumpat,confined streamlets,: carmina antro seclusa relinquit,.—Poet. mid.: ille sub extremā pendens secluditur alā, shuts himself off, i. e. protects himself, .—
In gen., to separate, sunder, shut off: cur luna queat terram secludere solis Lumine,: dextrum cornu, quod erat a sinistro seclusum,: cohors seclusa ab reliquis,fin.: ab suis interceptum et seclusum,: Caesar munitione flumen a monte seclusit,: mare Tyrrhenum a Lucrino molibus seclusum,: stabula ad eam rem seclusa,set apart,.—
Trop. *
To shut off, seclude: a libero spiritu atque a communi luce seclusum,.—
To separate, remove: corpore vitam, * : secludite curas, shut out, exclude, i. q. excludite, Serv.—Hence, sēclūsus, a, um, P. a., sundered, separated, remote, secluded: his devium quoddam iter esse seclusum a concilio deorum,: seclusum nemus,.—Absol.: in secluso,in a remote, secluded place,.—Comp., sup., and adv. do not occur.

la:noun:secta.gloss: a trodden or beaten way, pathway, mode, manner, method, principle
senses: a trodden or beaten way, pathway, mode, manner, method, principle
a body of political principles, party, side, faction
la:noun:secta.html:
secta, ae, f.
part. perf. of seco, sc. via, v. seco, I. C. 2., and II. B. fin.
; prop.,
a trodden or beaten way, a path; footsteps; hence, trop., a (prescribed) way, mode, manner, method, principles of conduct or procedure (syn.: ratio, via, etc.); most freq. in the phrase sectam (alicujus) sequi (persequi, etc.), to follow in the footsteps (of any one); hence, also, sectam (alicujus) secuti, a party, faction, sect.
In gen.: nos, qui hanc sectam rationemque vitae, re magis quam verbis, secuti sumus,mode of life,; so, vitae,; ; ; cf. : horum nos hominum sectam atque instituta persequimur,; cf.: cujus sectam sequi, cujus imperio parere potissimum vellet,: sequi ejus auctoritatem, cujus sectam atque imperium secutus est,: omnis natura habet quasi viam quandam et sectam quam sequatur,: negant se pro Vitruvio sectamque ejus secutis precatum venisse,; cf. ; ; ; 42, 31: juvenes hortatur, ut illam ire viam pergant et eidem incumbere sectae,: divitioris sectam plerumque secuntur Quamlibet et fortes,follow, adhere to,: gallae sectam meam exsecutae, mihi comites, etc., et saep.—
In partic., doctrines, school, sect (not freq. until the post-Aug. per.; syn.: schola, disciplina).
In philosophic lang.: quo magis tuum, Brute, judicium probo, qui eorum philosophorum sectam secutus es,; cf.: inter Stoicos et Epicuri sectam secutos pugna perpetua est,.— Plur.: ad morem certas in philosophia sectas sequendi,: neque me cujusdam sectae velut quādam superstitione imbutus addixi,: assumptā Stoicorum arrogantiā sectāque,: Demetrio Cynicam sectam professo,: auctoritatem Stoicae sectae praeferebat,; : inter duos diversarum sectarum velut duces,. —
In jurisprudence: hi duo primum veluti diversas sectas fecerunt,schools,.—
In medicine, a school: alia est Hippocratis secta, alia Asclepiadis,.—
In religion, a sect, : plurimae sectae et haereses,: Nazaraenorum,.—
Rarely of a class or guild of men: sincera et innoxia pastoriae illius sectae integritas,.—
In Appul., a band of robbers, , pp. 150, 29, and 153, 22.

sēcessus, ūs, m.

,
a going away, departure, separation (not ante-Aug.).
In gen. (very rare): avium,: quasi quodam secessu mentis atque animi facto a corpore,.—
In partic.
(Acc. to secedo, I. B. 1.) Retirement, solitude (the prevailing signif. of the word; syn. solitudo).
Lit.: carmina secessum scribentis et otia quaerunt,; cf.: medium tempus

in otio secessuque egit, : in secessu ruris sui Sabini, id. Fragm. Vit. Hor. fin.: silentium et secessus non semper possunt contingere,; ; ; ; ; ; ; : specie secessus exul,: unus e senatoribus Rhodii secessus comes,: gratum litus amoeni secessus, et saep.—

Transf., a retreat, recess: est in secessu longo locus, etc.,; ; ; cf. ; ; ; ; ; in plur., ; ; ; ; ; al.—Of a privy, .—
Trop. (very rare): ideoque mihi videtur M. Tullius tantum intulisse eloquentiae lumen, quod in hos quoque studiorum secessus excurrit, into these remote departments of study (i. e. remote from forensic debates), : in secessu quam in fronte beatior,in his own mind, inwardly,ext.—
(Acc. to secedo, I. B. 2.) For the usual secessio (II.), a political secession: iratae plebis secessus,.—
A place of retirement, privy, drain (late Lat.), ; .

la:noun:securitas.html:
sēcūrĭtas, ātis, f.
securus
,
freedom from care, unconcern, composure.
Lit.
In a good sense (class.): Democriti securitas, quae est animi tamquam tranquillitas, quam appellavit εὐθυμίαν, eo separanda fuit ab hac disputatione, quia ista animi tranquillitas ea ipsa est beata vita, : securitatem nunc appello vacuitatem aegritudinis, in quā vita beata posita est,: vacandum omni est animi perturbatione, ut tranquillitas animi et securitas assit, quae affert cum constantiam tum etiam dignitatem,: beatam vitam in animi securitate et in omnium vacatione munerum ponimus,; and 47; ; ; ; (opp. cura); (opp. timor); 7, 6, 14; 7, 10, 60; ; fin.; : securitas inaffectatae orationis,quietness,; cf.: vocis ac vultus,.—Plur. (opp. curae): somno ac securitatibus jam dudum hoc fuit,.—With gen. obj.: operosissima securitas mortis in M. Ofilio Hilaro ab antiquis traditur,.—
In a bad sense, carelessness, heedlessness, negligence (not till after the Aug. period; syn. incuria): neminem celerius opprimi quam qui nihil timeret et frequentissimum initium esse calamitatis securitatem,: res altera taedium laboris, altera securitatem parit,; ; ; 4, 1, 55; 6, 1, 34; 6, 3, 62; ; ; .—With gen. obj.: memoriae plerumque inhaeret fidelius, quod nullā scribendi securitate laxatur,.—
Transf., object., freedom from danger, safety, security (not till after the Aug. period): cum innumerabilia sint mortis signa, salutis securitatisque nulla sunt,: securitatis urbanae custos,: securitas securitate mutuā persciscenda est,; cf.: securitati ante quam vindictae consulere,: perpetua Romani imperii,: tutela securitatis,: nec spem modo ac votum securitas publica, sed ipsius voti fiduciam assumserit,: itinerum,: annonae,: somnum a repentinā securitate datum,: dextras securitatis,a safe conduct,.—Hence, SECVRITAS, personified as the tutelary goddess of the Roman State, and 1831.—
Mercant. t. t., a guarantee, security for a debt or obligation (by hypothecation, mortgage; by receipt or acknowledgment, etc.): id quod sibi debetur, consequi debet vel ejus securitatem, fin.—Plur., ;

One who practises, a follower (late Lat.): bonorum operum,.

Geometrical t. t., division, section: ut de ratione dividendi, de sectione in infinitum, etc.,.
